Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

altarr (development version)

  • Sparse arrays: altarr() takes a chunk index, present (a logical per chunk of the grid, or a matrix of the stored chunks’ coordinates), and a fill value. Absent chunks are never passed to fetch and never cached; every read of them gives fill. sum(), min() and max() of a double array count the absent cells from the index without touching them. altarr_stats() reports chunks_present and chunks_absent. Saved recipes carry the index; older recipes load with every chunk present.

  • altarr_present() and altarr_fill() return an array’s chunk index and fill value.

  • altarr_view(x, i, j, k) is x[i, j, k, drop = FALSE] as a new lazy array. A view of a sparse array is sparse: its chunk index is derived from its source’s, so nothing is read for the empty parts.

  • altarr_zarr_v2() lists the store once and uses the listing as the chunk index: unwritten chunks read as fill_value without being opened. altarr_example_zarr(sparse = TRUE) writes a store with only a diagonal band of chunks. Demo: inst/examples/sparse.R.

  • altarr() takes store_axes, for an array whose chunk grid is its store’s own: the R dimension of each stored axis, in store order (rev(seq_along(dim)) for a C-order store whose shape the array reverses). altarr_plan() then starts each row with the chunk’s key in the store, dim_0 .., the column names of byterefs views and zaro’s plans, so a plan joins to them; its own columns are unchanged. Without store_axes (the default) the plan has no keys, since altarr cannot know whether its grid is the store’s. altarr_zarr_v2() sets it. Saved recipes carry it; recipes saved by earlier versions load with it unset, and earlier versions load new recipes and ignore it.

altarr 0.1.1

First CRAN submission.

  • The Description says what the package does now (lazy chunked arrays used by ndr, zaro and GDAL7) rather than describing a prototype.

  • The blog post copy in inst/blog/ stays in the repository but is no longer installed with the package.

  • New vignette, vignette("fetch", package = "altarr"): writing a fetch function, for maintainers of Zarr, netCDF, GDAL and object-store readers.

  • pkgdown site at https://hypertidy.github.io/altarr/, built by GitHub Actions.

altarr 0.1.0

First release-shaped version: the package is usable on its own, not only as a record of the base R proposal (tag v0.0.1).

  • Bounded chunk cache: least recently used chunks are evicted to keep each array within getOption("altarr.cache_bytes") (default 256 MiB). A copy shares its original’s cache (#5, #10).
  • Planned region reads (ALTREP Get_region): mean(), prod(), anyNA() and reductions on R’s wrapper class read whole chunk layers in batched fetch calls instead of one chunk per round trip (#6, #11).
  • Integer and logical arrays, via altarr(type = ). altarr_zarr_v2() picks the type from the Zarr dtype; CF scale and offset give doubles (#7, #12).
  • ?altarr_contract documents the fetch contract, pinned sources, saving recipes safely, and a measured table of which base R operations are planned, element by element, or materializing (#8, #13).
  • New vignette, vignette("walkthrough", package = "altarr"): ten steps showing what base R asks a lazy array for.
  • Examples for every exported function; altarr_zarr_v2() is labelled a demonstration reader.
  • useDynLib is declared in roxygen, so document() keeps it (#14).
  • GitHub Actions R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows.

altarr 0.0.1

  • The state of the package for the base R ArraySubset hook proposal and the post “What R does today with an ALTREP that has a dim and no class”.
